property_summary: Invariant: calling receive() always increases depositsCount by exactly 1 and never decreases (i.e., depositsCount after a successful receive() is previous + 1); the mutant removing the safety check can allow an overflow wrap that violates this for some inputs.

For any payable call to receive() from any sender with any value, the contract's depositsCount never becomes less than the previous value (i.e., depositsCount_after >= depositsCount_before); removing the require allows an overflow when depositsCount is max uint, breaking this rule for some input.

For any payable call to receive(), the reference C prevents depositsCount from wrapping (i.e., if depositsCount == type(uint).max then receive() will revert), whereas the mutant increments unconditionally and thus allows depositsCount to overflow from max to 0 for some input sender/value, violating this safety.

The reference reverts when depositsCount is at uint256 max and receive() is invoked (preventing overflow), whereas the mutant increments unconditionally and therefore does not revert for that input, allowing depositsCount to wrap; the property: calling receive() when depositsCount == type(uint256).max always reverts on the reference but not on the mutant.

For any payable call to receive(), the reference contract prevents depositsCount from decreasing due to overflow by reverting when depositsCount == type(uint).max, so a call to receive() never results in a smaller depositsCount; the mutant removes that require and thus allows depositsCount to wrap from max to 0 for some inputs.

For any caller and any nonnegative ether amount sent to C.receive(), the reference contract always increments depositsCount and thus leaves depositsCount == 1 after a single funded receive call; the mutant that unconditionally reverts breaks this by reverting and leaving depositsCount unchanged (or the call failing).

For every payable call to receive with any sender and any nonzero or zero value, the reference contract always increments depositsCount by 1 (so depositsCount after the call equals prior+1); the mutant that uses a strict > check can revert on some inputs (e.g., when depositsCount==0) and thus not preserve this increment property.

For any payable call to C.receive, the reference contract always increases depositsCount by exactly 1 (so depositsCount after the call equals prior depositsCount + 1); the mutant using a strict > can revert for some inputs (e.g., when depositsCount == 0) and thus fails to preserve this increment property.

For any caller and any wei value sent, calling C's receive always increases depositsCount by 1 (the reference ensures depositsCount_after == depositsCount_before + 1); the mutant's stricter require can revert on some calls (so depositsCount does not increase), violating this rule.

For any caller and any nonzero ETH amount sent to C.receive, the reference C always accepts the payment and increases depositsCount by 1 (so depositsCount_after == depositsCount_before + 1); the mutant with a strict '>' require can revert for some inputs (notably when depositsCount == 0) and thus violates this rule for some fuzzed inputs.
